note: Real, weekly editorial Top 10 (Bill, 2026-09-25: build a modern replacement for The Ringer's old Weekly Top 10). General-audience — NOT derived from Bill's own Trakt data or BMTRE's scoring engine, and not personalized to him (it happens to overlap with shows he watches since those are genuinely the biggest shows on TV right now too). Normally auto-refreshed weekly via trakt/refresh_streaming_top10.py (a real Claude + web-search API call) — but this refresh (Oct 15, 2026) was done manually, inside an interactive Claude Code session via its own ordinary WebSearch tool, after the Anthropic API account ran out of credits mid-session (a real, confirmed HTTP 400 "credit balance too low" error) and Bill asked for a way to refresh without spending API credits. Same methodology, same currency discipline, same TMDB-resolution rule (never guess an id — a title WebSearch couldn't confidently resolve to a TMDB id ships with titleKey: null rather than a guess) — just researched by hand this one time, with a smaller pool (11, not the usual 25) given the manual effort involved. Every show's own status/predicted score/genre tags on the page are separately computed live from Bill's real Trakt data and BMTRE — display only, they never affect this list's editorial ranking. Every entry requires genuine current-week evidence (a recent episode/premiere/news event, cited in whyHere) before qualifying — a show whose season already wrapped with nothing new happening is excluded outright rather than kept around on reputation alone (this is exactly the rule the prior stale Reacher-led list should have triggered once its own data went 17 days out of date — see CLAUDE.md's Streaming Top 10 reliability-fix entry for the root cause). The normal automated weekly refresh resumes once API credits are restored.
methodology: Scored on four weighted dimensions, per Bill's own detailed brief: Audience 30% (is anyone actually watching — Nielsen minutes, JustWatch rank), Current Momentum 25% (is interest rising right now, not just sustained), Cultural Buzz 25% (is it being talked about — reviews, awards, entertainment press, viral moments), Watchability/Editorial Relevance 20% (is it actually a good recommendation this week — accessible, well-reviewed, worth starting). The raw score is an internal ranking mechanism only, never shown. Every entry keeps real, cited sources in the underlying data even though the page itself doesn't display them.

shows.title: East of Eden
shows.whyHere: Netflix's 7-episode Florence Pugh limited series (premiered Oct 1) took the #1 spot on the Global Top 10 English TV list in its opening week, with ~6.5 million views and a reported 200% jump in sales of Steinbeck's novel.
shows.whyWatch: Pugh's turn as the manipulative, magnetic Cathy Ames anchors a handsome, faithful adaptation that critics have praised (85-89% on Rotten Tomatoes).
shows.vibe: A sprawling, sun-scorched family tragedy with a viper at its center.
